tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

Goal: create a runnable Python backend skeleton and prove every dependency installs and imports, with pytest.

1. Use `uv` (0.12.11) with CPython 3.12: `cd backend && uv init --bare` (or write pyproject.toml by hand), `requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.13"`, then `uv venv --python 3.12` and `uv sync`. Commit `uv.lock`; do NOT commit `.venv`. Confirm `uv run python --version` prints 3.12.x, not the system 3.14.
2. Runtime deps: fastapi, uvicorn[standard], pydantic, pydantic-settings, sqlalchemy, httpx, langgraph, google-genai (the Google Gemini SDK), python-dotenv is NOT needed if pydantic-settings is used. Dev deps (uv dependency-group `dev`): pytest, pytest-asyncio (only if you need it), ruff.
3. 4. Tests in `backend/tests/`: (a) `/health` via FastAPI TestClient; (b) a dependency smoke test that imports fastapi, pydantic, sqlalchemy (and creates an in-memory SQLite engine and runs `SELECT 1`), httpx (use `httpx.MockTransport`, no network), langgraph (build and invoke a trivial 1-node StateGraph), google.genai (import only, no network); (c) a Settings test verifying defaults and that the API key is not exposed via repr. Tests must be offline and deterministic.
5. `backend/Dockerfile`: multi-stage using `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv` or `pip install uv`, python:3.12-slim base, installs with `uv sync --frozen --no-dev`, runs `uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port ${API_PORT:-9181}`, non-root user, and a `backend/.dockerignore`. Do not run docker build unless the docker daemon is up (`docker info` works); if you can't build it, say so.
6. Add `backend/README.md` with 6-10 lines: setup/run/test commands (`uv sync`, `uv run pytest`, `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run uvicorn app.main:app --port 9181`).
Ports: backend is 9181 (never 8000).

Verify (run and report actual output): `cd backend && uv sync && uv run pytest -q && uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .`, plus a quick `uv run uvicorn app.main:app --port 9181` start + `curl -s localhost:9181/health` then stop the server.

Report: your exact model name, changed files, exact commands run and their results, versions of installed key packages (from uv.lock), assumptions, and blockers. Do not mark the phase complete; the integrator does that.

3. Theme from env. Root `.env.example` defines, and Nuxt maps to `runtimeConfig.public.theme`:
   NUXT_PUBLIC_THEME_LIGHT_PRIMARY=#32a9e1, NUXT_PUBLIC_THEME_LIGHT_SECONDARY=#1e40af, NUXT_PUBLIC_THEME_LIGHT_BACKGROUND=#ffffff,
   NUXT_PUBLIC_THEME_DARK_PRIMARY=#7dd3fc, NUXT_PUBLIC_THEME_DARK_SECONDARY=#94a3b8, NUXT_PUBLIC_THEME_DARK_BACKGROUND=#020617.

Never print its contents.
   Inject the values as CSS custom properties (`--color-primary`, `--color-secondary`, `--color-background`) at the `:root` for light and under the dark scheme (support BOTH `prefers-color-scheme: dark` and a `data-theme="dark"|"light"` attribute override), rendered SSR-safe (e.g. `useHead` style/inline `:root` block generated from runtimeConfig, so there is no flash). Map them into Tailwind 4 `@theme inline` tokens so utilities like `bg-primary`, `text-secondary`, `bg-background` work. Add Vitest for the hex-validation/theme util with 2-4 unit tests (`bun run test` must pass offline).
6. `frontend/Dockerfile`: multi-stage (oven/bun for install+build, then a slim runtime running `node .output/server/index.mjs` on port 9180 with `NITRO_PORT`/`HOST=0.0.0.0`; theme/apiBase must remain overridable at container runtime via NUXT_PUBLIC_* env vars), non-root user, plus `frontend/.dockerignore`. input.content:
name: scmp-ai-assignment

# One-command deployment:  docker compose up --build
# Secrets and theme come from ./.env (copy .env.example first). The file is optional
# so `docker compose config` works on a fresh clone; the app then runs with defaults.

services:
  api:
    build:
      context: ./backend
    image: scmp-ai-assignment-api:local
    env_file:
      - path: .env
        required: false
    environment:
      API_PORT: "9181"
      # Persist SQLite in the named volume below (absolute path inside the container).
      DATABASE_URL: sqlite:////data/app.db
    ports:
      - "${API_PORT:-9181}:9181"
    volumes:
      - api-data:/data
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD
        - python
        - -c
        - "import urllib.request,sys; sys.exit(0 if urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:9181/health', timeout=3).status == 200 else 1)"
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 10s
    restart: unless-stopped

  web:
    build:
      context: ./frontend
    image: scmp-ai-assignment-web:local
    env_file:
      - path: .env
        required: false
    environment:
      HOST: 0.0.0.0
      NITRO_PORT: "9180"
    ports:
      - "${WEB_PORT:-9180}:9180"
    depends_on:
      api:
        condition: service_healthy
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  api-data:

## Development status

input.new_string:
## Development status

**Phase 0 (foundation) is complete:** repository, environment template, Python backend skeleton, Nuxt 4 frontend skeleton with env-driven theming, and Docker Compose deployment. The chat workflows, mock SSO, LangGraph agent, and approvals are added in later phases; this README is updated with each one.

## Deployment (Docker Compose)

Prerequisite: Docker Desktop (or Docker Engine) with the Compose plugin. Use `docker compose`, not `docker-compose`.

```bash
cp .env.example .env      # then edit .env and fill in the secrets (see below)
docker compose up --build
```

| Service | URL | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Frontend (Nuxt 4) | <http://localhost:9180> | Placeholder Phase 0 page with theme toggle |
| Backend (FastAPI) | <http://localhost:9181/health> | Returns `{"status":"ok"}`; interactive docs at `/docs` |

Useful commands:

```bash
docker compose up --build -d   # run in the background
docker compose ps              # both services should be Up; api should be (healthy)
docker compose logs -f         # follow logs
docker compose down            # stop; add -v to also delete the SQLite volume
```

The `web` service waits for the `api` healthcheck. SQLite is stored in the named volume `api-data` (mounted at `/app/data`), so data survives restarts.

### Configuration (`.env`)

`.env` is git-ignored and must never be committed. `.env.example` documents every variable.

| Variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `WEB_PORT` / `API_PORT` | Host ports for the frontend / backend (default `9180` / `9181`) |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_MODEL`, `GEMINI_THINKING_LEVEL` | Gemini provider (used from Phase 1; `LLM_PROVIDER=fake` for offline runs) |
| `REQRES_API_KEY`, `REQRES_BASE_URL` | Hosted ReqRes mock API; requires an `x-api-key` header |
| `NUXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE` | Backend URL as seen by the browser |
| `NUXT_PUBLIC_THEME_*` | Light and dark theme colours (see below) |

Changing `.env` needs `docker compose up -d` again (recreate) to take effect. The theme and API base are read by Nuxt at runtime, so no image rebuild is needed for them.

### Theme

| Token | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Primary | `#32a9e1` | `#7dd3fc` |
| Secondary | `#1e40af` | `#94a3b8` |
| Background | `#ffffff` | `#020617` |

Values are set through `NUXT_PUBLIC_THEME_{LIGHT,DARK}_{PRIMARY,SECONDARY,BACKGROUND}` and exposed as CSS variables and Tailwind tokens (`bg-primary`, `text-secondary`, `bg-background`). Invalid hex values fall back to the defaults. The toggle in the header switches light, dark, or system.

## Local development (without Docker)

Backend (Python 3.12 via `uv`):

```bash
cd backend
uv sync
uv run pytest -q
uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .
uv run uvicorn app.main:app --port 9181 --reload
```

Frontend (Bun):

```bash
cd frontend
bun install
bun run lint && bun run typecheck && bun run test
bun run dev                    # http://localhost:9180
```

Both dev servers read the shared repo-root `.env`, which is optional for Phase 0.

# SCMP Internal Operations AI Assistant

This repository contains a coding-assignment proof of concept for the AI Engineer (Internal Automation) role at South China Morning Post.

Repository URL: <https://github.com/SDCC-Ken/scmp-ai-assignment-2026-ken-chan-kwan-wing.git>

## Assignment objective

The PoC provides a unified employee self-service chat experience for two internal operations workflows:

- Leave Application
- Staff Claim

It demonstrates mock Google SSO, role-aware access, AI-assisted intent detection and structured field extraction, explicit confirmation before submission, mock enterprise API integration, approval workflows, and auditability.

All accounts, requests, dates, policies, and records are fictional demonstration data. No real SCMP, employee, HR, or financial data is used.

## Technology

- Nuxt 4, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS 4
- Python FastAPI, Pydantic, and LangGraph
- Google Gemini API with `gemini-3.8-flash` and low thinking
- SQLite and SQLAlchemy
- pytest, Playwright, and Docker Compose

## Engineering documentation

- [Agent engineering guide](AGENTS.md)
- [Agentic coding prompt log](PROMPT-INSTRUCTION.md)

## Development status

Phase 0 establishes the documented development constraints and project foundation. Setup, run, test, architecture, and demonstration instructions will be added alongside the working application so they remain accurate and reproducible.

**What I ran**

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Backend (Python 3.12.14) | 9 pytest tests pass; ruff check and format are clean |
| Frontend (Nuxt 4.5.2, Tailwind 4.3.3) | Lint, typecheck and 4 tests pass; build completed |
| `docker compose up --build` | `api` healthy at `localhost:9181/health`; `web` returned HTTP 200 at `localhost:9180` |
| Theme | All six hex values appear in the server-rendered page |

I stopped the stack afterwards (`docker compose down`). The frontend agent also checked that an environment override changes the output and that a bad value falls back to the default. I re-ran the tests and the compose stack myself rather than relying on the agents' reports.

**The seven steps**
1. **Repo:** `git init` on `main` with `origin` set to your GitHub URL.
2. **Environment files:** `.gitignore`, `.env` and `.env.example` are in place. `.env` is git-ignored and I never opened it, so add your `REQRES_API_KEY` and `GEMINI_API_KEY` there.
3. **Backend:** the backend agent built a FastAPI skeleton with `uv`.
4. **Frontend:** the frontend agent built a Nuxt 4 + Tailwind 4 skeleton.
5. **Theme:** your six colours are set through `NUXT_PUBLIC_THEME_*` variables, with a light/dark/system toggle.
6. **Docker Compose:** it runs the API on 9181 and the web app on 9180, and the web app waits for the API to be healthy.
7. **README:** it now has deployment, configuration, theme and local-development sections.

**Things you should know**
- **Commits:** I read "each phase of commit" as permission to commit locally. There are 5 commits, including the prompt-log commit. Nothing was pushed.
- **Nuxt version:** `AGENTS.md` and the README said Nuxt 3, so I changed both to Nuxt 4 to match your instruction.
- **Docker volume bug:** compose first mounted the SQLite volume at `/data`, which the non-root API user couldn't write to. I moved it to `/app/data` and confirmed it is writable.
- **TypeScript pin:** the frontend agent pinned TypeScript to 6.0 because 7.x breaks typescript-eslint.

- **Git author:** the repo is committing as `Ken Chan <wingwingchan2002@gmail.com>`, from your global git config. That differs from your job-application email, so change it if that's not intended.

To test it yourself:

```bash
docker compose up --build
```

Then open <http://localhost:9180> and <http://localhost:9181/health>. Tell me when you're ready and I'll start Phase 1.

Your run confirms Phase 0 works on your machine too.

- **Images:** both built (from cache, since I had already built them).
- **API:** it started on 9181 and answered every `/health` check with 200.
- **Web:** it is listening on 9180.

The repeated `GET /health` lines are Compose's own healthcheck, which runs every 10 seconds, so they will keep scrolling. The one `/health` request followed by a `/favicon.ico` 404 looks like you opening the page in a browser. The 404 is harmless because the API has no favicon. Its source address (`151.101.64.223`) looked odd to me, but it is most likely your local proxy or VPN, since the container only sees the gateway's address.

Press `Ctrl+C` in that terminal to stop it, or run `docker compose down` from another one. Compose ran in the foreground, so the containers stop when you interrupt it. The SQLite volume is kept unless you add `-v`.

When you have checked <http://localhost:9180> (light/dark toggle and the six colours) and are happy, say so and I'll start Phase 1. If anything looks off, tell me what you see and I'll fix it first.

content.text: Shared inputs are in place. Now the two bounded agents, with a written API contract so they can work in parallel.

input.description: Phase 1 backend DB and auth
input.prompt:
Phase: 1 - Database, seed data, real JWT auth
Role: backend
Repo root: /Users/kenchan/Documents/job-helper/scmp-ai-assignment/submission-docs. Read AGENTS.md there first (product scope + safety rules), then look at the existing backend/ skeleton (app/main.py, app/config.py, tests/).
File ownership: ONLY `backend/` (you may edit backend/pyproject.toml, uv.lock, backend/README.md, and everything under backend/app and backend/tests). The file backend/app/data/hk_public_holidays_1823.ics already exists (official 1823.gov.hk iCal, 2025-2027, fetched 2026-09-25) - use it, don't modify it.
Do NOT edit: root README.md, .env, .env.example, docker-compose.yml, AGENTS.md, PROMPT-INSTRUCTION.md, frontend/. Do NOT read or print `.env`. Do NOT run git commit/push. Do NOT call ReqRes or Gemini. Tests must be offline and must not depend on the real ../.env (build Settings with `_env_file=None` / explicit values). The only allowed network call is none - the holiday import command may fetch from 1823.gov.hk when a user runs it, but tests must use inline fixtures.

Everything is FICTIONAL demo data. Use emails at `example.com` (e.g. amy.lau@example.com) - email-validator rejects the `.example` TLD.

## A. Database layer (SQLAlchemy 2.x, SQLite, "safe")
- `app/db/` : `base.py` (DeclarativeBase), `session.py` (engine factory + `get_db` FastAPI dependency; sessions closed properly), models. Keep DB models, Pydantic API schemas (`app/schemas/`), and domain logic (`app/domain/`) in separate modules.
- SQLite safety: on every connection set `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`, `journal_mode=WAL` (skip WAL for :memory:), `busy_timeout=5000`, `synchronous=NORMAL`; `check_same_thread=False`; all access via ORM/bound params (never string-formatted SQL); create the parent directory of a file DB; tests use in-memory (StaticPool) or tmp_path files.
- All timestamps timezone-aware UTC (use a TypeDecorator so SQLite round-trips tz-aware values). Money must not lose precision (use Decimal end to end; test `Decimal("12.30")` round-trips, no float; avoid SQLAlchemy's Decimal-on-SQLite warning).
- String enums stored as VARCHAR with CHECK constraints (native_enum=False, create_constraint=True). Add sensible indexes (FKs, unique users.email, unique users.google_subject, unique public_holidays.holiday_date, (employee_id,status) on requests, (recipient_user_id,read_at) on notifications, (entity_type,entity_id) on audit_events).
- Tables and columns (exactly these names; additions are marked NEW):
  users: id, google_subject, email, display_name, role (employee|hr_approver|finance_approver), is_active, created_at
  conversations: id, user_id, status (active|closed), active_request_type (leave|claim|NULL), created_at, updated_at
  conversation_messages: id, conversation_id, sender_type (user|assistant|system), content, ui_metadata_json (JSON, nullable), created_at
  leave_requests: id, employee_id, leave_type (annual|sick|personal|unpaid), start_date, end_date, NEW start_day_part, NEW end_day_part (full|am|pm), calendar_days, working_days, status, required_approver_role, submitted_at, reviewed_by_user_id, reviewed_at, reviewer_note, created_at, updated_at
  claim_requests: id, employee_id, claim_type (travel|meal|equipment|training|other), amount, currency (default 'HKD'), receipt_date, status, required_approver_role, submitted_at, reviewed_by_user_id, reviewed_at, reviewer_note, created_at, updated_at
  external_submissions: id, request_type (leave|claim), request_id, provider ('reqres'), status (success|failed), http_status, external_reference_id, response_summary_json (JSON), error_message, submitted_at
  notifications: id, recipient_user_id, event_type, request_type, request_id, read_at, created_at
  audit_events: id, actor_user_id (nullable - failed logins / system), entity_type, entity_id, event_type, from_status, to_status, metadata_json (JSON), created_at
  public_holidays: id, holiday_date (unique), name, source (seed_2026|1823_ics), source_updated_at, created_at
  feedback: id, user_id, conversation_id (nullable), rating (CHECK 1..5), comment, created_at
  external_submissions.request_id / audit_events.entity_id / notifications.request_id are polymorphic (no FK); document that in a docstring and validate in the service layer.
- Create tables with `Base.metadata.create_all` (no Alembic) via `init_db()`. On app startup (lifespan) call init_db, and if `settings.db_auto_seed` is true AND the users table is empty, run the seed. Failures in startup seeding must log and not crash the API.
- Add settings (pydantic-settings, env names in root .env.example): `DB_AUTO_SEED` (bool, default true), `JWT_SECRET_KEY` (SecretStr, default empty), `JWT_EXPIRE_MINUTES` (default 60), `JWT_ISSUER` (default scmp-ai-assignment), `MOCK_SSO_ENABLED` (default true). Empty JWT secret in non-production -> generate a random per-process secret and log a warning (never log the secret); APP_ENV=production with a secret shorter than 32 chars -> raise at startup. Existing settings tests must still pass.

## B. Domain rules (pure functions, no DB/FastAPI imports) in `app/domain/`
1. Request status enum: draft, pending_approval, submission_failed, approved, rejected, cancelled. Transition table (state machine): draft->pending_approval, draft->submission_failed, draft->cancelled, submission_failed->pending_approval, submission_failed->cancelled, pending_approval->approved, pending_approval->rejected. approved/rejected/cancelled are terminal. Provide `can_transition`, `assert_transition` (raises a typed domain error), and a helper that applies a transition to a request object and returns the audit-event fields (from_status, to_status). Rejecting requires a non-empty reviewer_note; approving/rejecting requires an actor who may review (below) and that actor is not the request's employee.
2. Role resolution: `required_approver_role(request_type)` leave->hr_approver, claim->finance_approver. `can_review(user, request_type)`: HR only leave, Finance only claim, employee never; inactive users never. `can_view_request(user, request)`: employee only their own; approvers only their request type. Also `resolve_role(email, users)` helper to find the active user + role by case-insensitive email.
3. Leave day calculation with HALF-DAY support. Working week is Mon-Fri; Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays (from the public_holidays table) do not count. `start_day_part` / `end_day_part` in {full, am, pm}. Rules: single-day leave -> start_date == end_date and start_day_part == end_day_part (full = 1 day, am or pm = 0.5). Multi-day leave -> start_day_part in {full, pm} (pm = starts afternoon, counts 0.5 on that date) and end_day_part in {full, am} (am = ends at noon, counts 0.5 on that date). A half-day on a weekend/holiday counts 0. working_days is a Decimal in 0.5 steps; calendar_days uses the same half-day adjustment over calendar dates. Zero working days -> validation error. end_date < start_date -> error. Return a small result object. This is how a user "applies half-day leave"; keep it easy for the later LLM extraction step to fill (two optional fields, default full).
4. Pydantic input models for later phases: `LeaveDraft` (employee_email, leave_type, start_date, end_date, start_day_part=full, end_day_part=full) and `ClaimDraft` (employee_email, claim_type, amount > 0 with max 2 decimal places, currency HKD, receipt_date not in the future). Keep them separate from DB models.

## C. Public holidays and CLI
- `app/services/holidays.py`: parse the 1823 iCal text (handle line folding, `DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:YYYYMMDD`, SUMMARY escapes, curly apostrophes), `upsert_holidays(session, events, source, source_updated_at)` idempotent by holiday_date, `fetch_1823_ics(client)` using httpx (timeout, raises a clear error) from https://www.1823.gov.hk/common/ical/en.ics, `is_working_day`, and a function to load holidays as a set for a date range.
- The seed loads the bundled `app/data/hk_public_holidays_1823.ics` for years 2026 and 2027 only, with source `seed_2026` (bundled snapshot verified against 1823 and gov.hk on 2026-09-25) and source_updated_at from the file's DTSTAMP max (2026-05-15). The import command writes source `1823_ics`.
- `app/cli.py` using argparse (no new dependency), run as `uv run python -m app.cli <command>`: `init-db`; `seed [--reset --yes]` (idempotent; --reset drops everything and requires --yes); `import-holidays [--year YYYY ...] [--file PATH] [--url URL]` (fetch from 1823 by default, or from a local .ics; if a requested year is absent from the feed, exit non-zero with a clear message saying 1823 publishes about 3 years ahead; print counts inserted/updated). ## D. Seed data (`app/seed.py`, `seed_demo_data(session, today: date | None = None)`)

Empty JWT secret in non-production -> generate a random per-process secret and log a warning (never log the secret); APP_ENV=production with a secret shorter than 32 chars -> raise at startup. Existing settings tests must still pass.

## B. Domain rules (pure functions, no DB/FastAPI imports) in `app/domain/`
1. Request status enum: draft, pending_approval, submission_failed, approved, rejected, cancelled. Transition table (state machine): draft->pending_approval, draft->submission_failed, draft->cancelled, submission_failed->pending_approval, submission_failed->cancelled, pending_approval->approved, pending_approval->rejected. approved/rejected/cancelled are terminal. Provide `can_transition`, `assert_transition` (raises a typed domain error), and a helper that applies a transition to a request object and returns the audit-event fields (from_status, to_status). Rejecting requires a non-empty reviewer_note; approving/rejecting requires an actor who may review (below) and that actor is not the request's employee.
2. Role resolution: `required_approver_role(request_type)` leave->hr_approver, claim->finance_approver. `can_review(user, request_type)`: HR only leave, Finance only claim, employee never; inactive users never. `can_view_request(user, request)`: employee only their own; approvers only their request type. Also `resolve_role(email, users)` helper to find the active user + role by case-insensitive email.
3. Leave day calculation with HALF-DAY support. Working week is Mon-Fri; Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays (from the public_holidays table) do not count. `start_day_part` / `end_day_part` in {full, am, pm}. Rules: single-day leave -> start_date == end_date and start_day_part == end_day_part (full = 1 day, am or pm = 0.5). Multi-day leave -> start_day_part in {full, pm} (pm = starts afternoon, counts 0.5 on that date) and end_day_part in {full, am} (am = ends at noon, counts 0.5 on that date). A half-day on a weekend/holiday counts 0. working_days is a Decimal in 0.5 steps; calendar_days uses the same half-day adjustment over calendar dates. Zero working days -> validation error. end_date < start_date -> error. Return a small result object. This is how a user "applies half-day leave"; keep it easy for the later LLM extraction step to fill (two optional fields, default full).
4. Pydantic input models for later phases: `LeaveDraft` (employee_email, leave_type, start_date, end_date, start_day_part=full, end_day_part=full) and `ClaimDraft` (employee_email, claim_type, amount > 0 with max 2 decimal places, currency HKD, receipt_date not in the future). Keep them separate from DB models.

## C. Public holidays and CLI
- `app/services/holidays.py`: parse the 1823 iCal text (handle line folding, `DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:YYYYMMDD`, SUMMARY escapes, curly apostrophes), `upsert_holidays(session, events, source, source_updated_at)` idempotent by holiday_date, `fetch_1823_ics(client)` using httpx (timeout, raises a clear error) from https://www.1823.gov.hk/common/ical/en.ics, `is_working_day`, and a function to load holidays as a set for a date range.
- The seed loads the bundled `app/data/hk_public_holidays_1823.ics` for years 2026 and 2027 only, with source `seed_2026` (bundled snapshot verified against 1823 and gov.hk on 2026-09-25) and source_updated_at from the file's DTSTAMP max (2026-05-15). The import command writes source `1823_ics`.
- `app/cli.py` using argparse (no new dependency), run as `uv run python -m app.cli <command>`: `init-db`; `seed [--reset --yes]` (idempotent; --reset drops everything and requires --yes); `import-holidays [--year YYYY ...] [--file PATH] [--url URL]` (fetch from 1823 by default, or from a local .ics; if a requested year is absent from the feed, exit non-zero with a clear message saying 1823 publishes about 3 years ahead; print counts inserted/updated). Document the yearly procedure in backend/README.md, including the Docker form `docker compose exec api python -m app.cli import-holidays --year 2028`.

## D. Seed data (`app/seed.py`, `seed_demo_data(session, today: date | None = None)`)
Deterministic given `today`. Idempotent (no-op if users exist). Counts:
- Users 5: 3 employees, 1 hr_approver, 1 finance_approver; fictional names, `@example.com` emails, `google_subject` like `mock-google-sub-001`, all active.
- Leave requests 10: 2 pending_approval (future dates), 1 recent approved, 1 recent rejected (with reviewer_note), the remaining 6 past-dated history (approved, plus at most one rejected). Include at least one single-day half-day (am) leave and one multi-day leave starting pm, with correctly computed calendar_days/working_days using the seeded holidays. required_approver_role = hr_approver, reviewed_by = the HR user for reviewed ones, submitted_at set for all non-draft.
- Claim requests 10: same status mix, required_approver_role = finance_approver, reviewed by the Finance user, HKD amounts, receipt_dates in the past.
- Audit events 12-16 total covering: request creation, confirmation, external submission success, approval, rejection, and at least one failure (an external submission `failed` with http_status 429 or 500 followed by a successful retry for a request that is now pending_approval), plus matching external_submissions rows (provider reqres, success rows carry a fake external_reference_id like `mock-ref-...` and never real API output). Every audit row's from/to status must be a legal transition from the state machine.
- Conversations 2-3 with 2-5 short messages each (one user asking for leave, one for a claim), ui_metadata_json on some assistant messages.
- Also seed a few notifications (approvers notified of pending items) and 1-2 feedback rows. Keep this modest.
- Reviewer notes and messages are fictional and short. Nothing resembling real SCMP/HR data.

## E. Real auth (PyJWT) - API contract, the frontend agent is coding against this exactly
Add deps with uv: `pyjwt`, `email-validator` (or pydantic[email]). Code in `app/auth/` and `app/api/routes/`. Mount everything under `/api`. Keep `GET /health` at its current path.
- `GET /api/auth/mock-users` -> 200 JSON list of the active seed users: `[{"id":1,"email":"...","display_name":"...","role":"employee"}]`, ordered employees, hr_approver, finance_approver. Never include google_subject. If MOCK_SSO_ENABLED is false -> 404.
- `POST /api/auth/mock-google/login` body `{"email":"amy.lau@example.com"}` -> 200 `{"access_token":"<jwt>","token_type":"bearer","expires_in":3600,"user":{"id","email","display_name","role"}}`. Unknown email -> 401 `{"detail":"Invalid credentials"}` (same message as any other failure - no user enumeration); inactive user -> 403 `{"detail":"Account is inactive"}`; MOCK_SSO_ENABLED false -> 404. Writes audit event `auth.login` (entity_type user) or `auth.login_failed` (actor null, metadata has the attempted email only when the user exists is NOT required - keep it minimal and never store tokens).
- `GET /api/auth/me` with `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` -> 200 `{"id","email","display_name","role"}`; missing/invalid/expired token -> 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`; inactive user -> 403.
- `POST /api/auth/logout` (Bearer) -> 204, writes audit `auth.logout`. Tokens are stateless, so the client discards them; say so in a docstring.
- JWT: HS256, claims `sub` (user id as string), `email`, `role`, `iss`, `iat`, `exp`, `jti`; verify signature, exp, iss and required claims; reject `alg: none` and wrong algorithms. The user (and their role and is_active) is ALWAYS re-loaded from the DB on each request; the token role claim is informational only, so a demoted or deactivated user loses access immediately.
- Reusable FastAPI dependencies: `get_current_user`, `require_roles(*roles)` (403 for wrong role). Do not add leave/claim business endpoints (later phase); exercise `require_roles` in tests with a tiny router defined in the tests only.
- CORS is already configured from CORS_ORIGINS; make sure the `Authorization` header is allowed.

## F. Tests (pytest, offline, deterministic; the assignment's Definition of Done needs these)
Add tests with each behaviour: model constraints (CHECK on role/status, FK enforcement actually on via PRAGMA, unique email, rating range, Decimal precision, tz-aware round-trip); seed (exact counts above, status mix, idempotent second run, all audit transitions legal, half-day rows present with right working_days, holidays for 2026 and 2027 = 17 each, no real-looking data, all emails end with @example.com); role resolution (required approver, can_review matrix for all 3 roles x 2 types incl. inactive user, can_view_request, self-approval blocked); state transitions (every allowed edge, every disallowed edge from every state, terminal states, reject needs note); leave-day calculation (full day, am/pm half-day, multi-day with pm start/am end, weekend skip, public holiday skip e.g. 2026-10-01 National Day, invalid combos, zero-day error, year boundary); holiday ICS parsing and idempotent upsert with an inline fixture; CLI commands via function calls on a tmp DB (seed idempotent, --reset needs --yes, import-holidays --file); auth API (mock-users list, login success for each of 3 roles, unknown email 401, inactive 403, MOCK_SSO_ENABLED false 404, /me ok, expired token, tampered signature, alg none, wrong issuer, deactivated user rejected with a still-valid token, role demotion takes effect immediately, require_roles matrix, audit rows written, no google_subject leaked). Use FastAPI `dependency_overrides` and a per-test in-memory DB.

## Verify (run and report actual output)
`cd backend && uv sync && uv run pytest -q && uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .`
Then a real smoke: `DATABASE_URL=sqlite:///./data/smoke.db APP_ENV=development uv run uvicorn app.main:app --port 9181` (data/ is git-ignored; delete smoke.db afterwards), `curl` mock-users and a login and /me with the returned token, then stop the server and confirm port 9181 is free.
Also confirm `uv run python -m app.cli seed --reset --yes` and `import-holidays --file app/data/hk_public_holidays_1823.ics --year 2026` work on a temp DB. Do NOT hit the live 1823 URL in tests; one manual live `import-holidays --year 2027` against a temp DB is fine and encouraged (report the result).

Report: your exact model name, changed files, commands run and real results, table list with row counts after seeding, the final API contract if you deviated anywhere (say exactly where and why), assumptions (e.g. leave/claim type lists), and blockers. Do not mark the phase complete; the integrator does.

Phase: 1 - Mock Google sign-in UI wired to real JWT auth
Role: frontend
Repo root: /Users/kenchan/Documents/job-helper/scmp-ai-assignment/submission-docs. Read AGENTS.md there first, briefly, then the existing frontend/ (Nuxt 4, Tailwind CSS 4, Bun, env-driven theme with bg-primary / text-secondary / bg-background tokens, dark mode via data-theme + prefers-color-scheme).
File ownership: ONLY `frontend/`.
Do NOT edit: root README.md, .env, .env.example, docker-compose.yml, AGENTS.md, PROMPT-INSTRUCTION.md, backend/. Do NOT read or print `.env`. Do NOT run git commit/push.

Goal: a "Sign in with Google (MOCK)" experience that lists the 5 fictional seed users across the 3 roles, warns clearly that it is a mock, signs in as the chosen user through the REAL backend JWT API, protects pages, and shows a role-aware home page. The backend agent is building the API in parallel - code against this exact contract:

- `GET  {api}/api/auth/mock-users` -> 200 `[{"id":1,"email":"amy.lau@example.com","display_name":"Amy Lau","role":"employee"}, ...]` (ordered employees, hr_approver, finance_approver). 404 when mock SSO is disabled.
- `POST {api}/api/auth/mock-google/login` body `{"email":"..."}` -> 200 `{"access_token","token_type":"bearer","expires_in":3600,"user":{"id","email","display_name","role"}}`; 401 `{"detail":"Invalid credentials"}`; 403 `{"detail":"Account is inactive"}`; 404 when disabled.
- `GET  {api}/api/auth/me` with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` -> 200 user object; 401/403 otherwise.
- `POST {api}/api/auth/logout` with Bearer -> 204 (best-effort; always clear the local session even if it fails).
- Roles: `employee`, `hr_approver`, `finance_approver`.
- Base URLs: browser uses `runtimeConfig.public.apiBase` (env NUXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE, default http://localhost:9181). During SSR inside Docker, `localhost` is the web container itself, so add a PRIVATE runtimeConfig key `apiBaseServer` (env NUXT_API_BASE_SERVER; docker-compose sets it to http://api:9181) and use `import.meta.server ? (config.apiBaseServer || config.public.apiBase) : config.public.apiBase`. Do not expose apiBaseServer in `public`.

Requirements:
1. RESEARCH FIRST (WebSearch/WebFetch): find Google's official "Sign in with Google" branding guidelines and the standard Google account-chooser layout (button variants, the multicolour "G" mark, min sizes, text "Sign in with Google", Roboto font, light/dark/neutral button themes, what you must not alter). Follow them for the button, and model the account chooser (avatar with initials, name, email, list rows, "Use another account" is NOT needed) on that layout. Report the source URLs. Because this is a mock, do not use the phrase "Continue as" in a way that implies real Google authentication, and never load Google scripts or make any request to Google - draw the G mark as an inline SVG.
2. Route `/login` (layout without the authenticated header): app title, short explanation, a prominent MOCK warning banner that is visible BEFORE any click and says, in plain words, that this is a demonstration-only mock sign-in, not connected to Google, and that choosing an account signs you in immediately as that fictional user (no password). Use `role="alert"`/appropriate semantics, an amber/yellow warning style with sufficient contrast in BOTH light and dark themes (verify contrast >= 4.5:1 for text; use fixed amber utility colours, the theme tokens only cover primary/secondary/background).
3. Clicking the "Sign in with Google" button opens an accessible modal account chooser (`role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, labelled title, focus moves in and is trapped, Escape and backdrop click close it, focus returns to the button). The chooser repeats a short mock warning, shows loading / error / empty states for `GET /api/auth/mock-users`, and lists the 5 users grouped or labelled by role with initials avatar, display name, email and a role badge (Employee, HR Approver, Finance Approver). Clicking a user calls the login API, shows a per-row loading state, disables other rows, surfaces errors (401/403/network) without a crash, then navigates to `/`. Keyboard operable throughout.
4. Auth state: a `useAuth` composable and cookie storage of the JWT via `useCookie` (name `auth-token`, `sameSite: 'lax'`, `secure` only when served over https, maxAge from `expires_in`). Keep user in `useState`. Global route middleware: unauthenticated -> `/login`; authenticated visiting `/login` -> `/`. On app load validate the token via `/api/auth/me` (server-side too, using the server base URL); on 401 clear the cookie and redirect to `/login`. Add an `$fetch` wrapper (`useApi`) that adds the Bearer header and auto-signs-out on 401. No token in URLs or logs, and do not put the token in the persisted `useState`/payload (only the user object).
5. Home `/` (protected): header with app name, user chip (name + role badge), theme toggle (already exists), Sign out button. Body: "Signed in as <name> (<role>)" plus a role capability card taken from AGENTS.md product scope - Employee: create Leave Application and Staff Claim, view own requests; HR Approver: list/view/approve/reject Leave requests only; Finance Approver: list/view/approve/reject Claim requests only - each marked "coming in the next phase", and a clear "Mock session" reminder. No chat yet.
6. Put pure logic (role labels, capability map, initials, cookie maxAge, error-message mapping) in `app/utils/` and cover it with Vitest (>= 8 meaningful tests, offline). Keep the existing theme tests passing. Also make the mock-warning text a single constant reused by page and modal.
7. Quality: `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test`, `bun run build` must all pass. Responsive down to 360px wide; visible focus rings; respects the light/dark tokens; no hydration warnings (check the dev/preview console).
8. For verification without waiting for the backend: write a tiny throwaway stub of the contract (e.g. a Bun script under the scratchpad or `frontend/scripts/` - if you keep it in the repo name it `scripts/mock-api-stub.ts` and document it in frontend/README.md as a dev aid only, port 9181), run the built app against it, and exercise: /login shows the warning, the chooser lists 5 users, choosing a user lands on `/`, reload keeps the session (SSR), sign out returns to /login, a 401 from /me forces sign-out. Use curl for SSR checks; if a browser tool is available, also take a light and dark screenshot of /login and the chooser and check the console is clean. Stop all servers afterwards and confirm ports 9180/9181 are free.
9. Update frontend/README.md (short) with the auth flow and the stub. The Dockerfile must keep working; NUXT_API_BASE_SERVER is a runtime env var.

Report: your exact model name, changed files, Google branding sources you followed, exact commands run and results, key decisions/assumptions (cookie vs storage tradeoff: state it honestly, e.g. the JS-set cookie is readable by page scripts so it is not httpOnly), any contract deviations or things you need from the backend, and blockers. Do not mark the phase complete; the integrator does.

Because this is a mock, do not use the phrase "Continue as" in a way that implies real Google authentication, and never load Google scripts or make any request to Google - draw the G mark as an inline SVG.
2. Route `/login` (layout without the authenticated header): app title, short explanation, a prominent MOCK warning banner that is visible BEFORE any click and says, in plain words, that this is a demonstration-only mock sign-in, not connected to Google, and that choosing an account signs you in immediately as that fictional user (no password). Use `role="alert"`/appropriate semantics, an amber/yellow warning style with sufficient contrast in BOTH light and dark themes (verify contrast >= 4.5:1 for text; use fixed amber utility colours, the theme tokens only cover primary/secondary/background).
3. Clicking the "Sign in with Google" button opens an accessible modal account chooser (`role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, labelled title, focus moves in and is trapped, Escape and backdrop click close it, focus returns to the button). content.text:
Both Phase 1 agents are running in parallel: backend (database, seed data, holidays, JWT auth) and frontend (mock Google sign-in), each confined to its own directory. The shared files are already in place: holiday data, `.env.example` and compose.

While I wait, here are the decisions I made on your behalf, so you can push back.

- **Half-day leave.** I added two columns to `leave_requests`: `start_day_part` and `end_day_part` (`full`, `am` or `pm`). `working_days` becomes a decimal in 0.5 steps.
  - A single half day is `am` or `pm` on one date and counts 0.5.
  - A multi-day leave can start in the afternoon (`pm`) or end at noon (`am`).
  - The chat step later only has to fill two optional fields.
- **Working week.** Monday to Friday, minus Hong Kong public holidays.
- **Holiday data.** 2026 and 2027 each have 17 dates, and I checked them against both the 1823 calendar and the gov.hk pages. They load as `seed_2026`; the yearly import command writes `1823_ics`.
- **Extra login auditing.** Login, failed login and logout are written to `audit_events`, because it costs almost nothing.
- **Leave and claim type lists.** Leave types are annual, sick, personal and unpaid. Claim types are travel, meal, equipment, training and other. Tell me if you want different ones.
- **JWT secret.** With `JWT_SECRET_KEY` empty in development, the backend uses a random per-process secret, so logins reset when the API restarts. Production mode refuses to start without a real secret.

I'll integrate, run the whole stack in a browser, update the README and the prompt log, and commit once both agents report back.

"""JWT (HS256) creation and verification. Never log tokens or the secret."""

import logging
import secrets
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from typing import Any
from uuid import uuid4

import jwt

from app.config import Settings

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

ALGORITHM = "HS256"
MIN_PRODUCTION_SECRET_LENGTH = 32
REQUIRED_CLAIMS = ["sub", "email", "role", "iss", "iat", "exp", "jti"]
CLOCK_SKEW_SECONDS = 5


class TokenError(Exception):
    """The bearer token is missing claims, expired, tampered with, or otherwise invalid."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TokenClaims:

"""Reusable FastAPI auth dependencies.

The user, role and ``is_active`` flag are ALWAYS re-read from the database. The role claim
inside the token is informational only, so demoting or deactivating a user takes effect on
their very next request.
"""

from collections.abc import Callable

from fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, Request, status
from fastapi.security import HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, HTTPBearer
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.auth.tokens import TokenError, decode_access_token
from app.db.models import User
from app.db.session import get_db
from app.domain.enums import UserRole

_bearer = HTTPBearer(auto_error=False)


def _unauthorized() -> HTTPException:
    return HTTPException(
        status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
        detail="Invalid or expired token",
        headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"},
    )


def get_current_user(
    request: Request,
    credentials: HTTPAuthorizationCredentials | None = Depends(_bearer),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
) -> User:
    if credentials is None or not credentials.credentials:
        raise _unauthorized()
    settings = request.app.state.settings
    try:
        claims = decode_access_token(
            credentials.credentials,
            secret=request.app.state.jwt_secret,
            issuer=settings.jwt_issuer,
        )
    except TokenError:
        raise _unauthorized() from None
    user = db.get(User, claims.user_id)
    if user is None:
        raise _unauthorized()
    if not user.is_active:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN, detail="Account is inactive")
    return user


def require_roles(*roles: UserRole) -> Callable[..., User]:
    """Dependency factory: 403 unless the current user's (DB) role is one of ``roles``."""
    allowed = frozenset(UserRole(r) for r in roles)

    def dependency(user: User = Depends(get_current_user)) -> User:
        if user.role not in allowed:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN, detail="Forbidden")
        return user

    return dependency
"""Mock Google SSO and session endpoints (mounted under /api/auth)."""

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, Request, Response, status
from sqlalchemy import func, select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.auth.dependencies import get_current_user
from app.auth.tokens import create_access_token
from app.db.models import User
from app.db.session import get_db
from app.domain.enums import UserRole
from app.schemas.auth import LoginRequest, TokenResponse, UserPublic
from app.services.audit import record_audit

router = APIRouter(prefix="/auth", tags=["auth"])

_ROLE_ORDER = {UserRole.EMPLOYEE: 0, UserRole.HR_APPROVER: 1, UserRole.FINANCE_APPROVER: 2}


def _require_mock_sso(request: Request) -> None:
    if not request.app.state.settings.mock_sso_enabled:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND, detail="Not Found")


@router.get("/mock-users", response_model=list[UserPublic])
def list_mock_users(
    _: None = Depends(_require_mock_sso), db: Session = Depends(get_db)
) -> list[User]:
    """Active fictional seed users: employees, then HR approver, then Finance approver."""
    users = db.scalars(select(User).where(User.is_active.is_(True))).all()
    return sorted(users, key=lambda u: (_ROLE_ORDER[u.role], u.id))


@router.post("/mock-google/login", response_model=TokenResponse)
def mock_google_login(
    body: LoginRequest,
    request: Request,
    _: None = Depends(_require_mock_sso),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
) -> TokenResponse:
    """Sign in as a seeded user without a password (mock Google SSO).

    Every failure looks the same (401 "Invalid credentials") except an inactive account
    (403). Audit rows never contain tokens.
    """
    user = db.scalar(select(User).where(func.lower(User.email) == body.email))
    if user is None:
        record_audit(
            db,
            entity_type="user",
            entity_id=None,
            event_type="auth.login_failed",
            metadata={"reason": "unknown_user"},
        )
        db.commit()
        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, detail="Invalid credentials")
    if not user.is_active:
        record_audit(
            db,
            entity_type="user",
            entity_id=user.id,
            event_type="auth.login_failed",
            metadata={"reason": "inactive"},
        )
        db.commit()
        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN, detail="Account is inactive")

    settings = request.app.state.settings
    token = create_access_token(
        user_id=user.id,
        email=user.email,
        role=user.role.value,
        secret=request.app.state.jwt_secret,
        issuer=settings.jwt_issuer,
        expires_minutes=settings.jwt_expire_minutes,
    )
    record_audit(
        db,
        entity_type="user",
        entity_id=user.id,
        event_type="auth.login",
        actor_user_id=user.id,
    )
    db.commit()
    return TokenResponse(
        access_token=token,
        expires_in=settings.jwt_expire_minutes * 60,
        user=UserPublic.model_validate(user),
    )


@router.get("/me", response_model=UserPublic)
def me(user: User = Depends(get_current_user)) -> User:
    """The signed-in user, freshly loaded from the database."""
    return user


@router.post("/logout", status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT)
def logout(user: User = Depends(get_current_user), db: Session = Depends(get_db)) -> Response:
    """Record the logout in the audit trail.

    Tokens are stateless (no server-side session or deny-list), so the client discards
    its token; it simply expires at ``exp``.
    """
    record_audit(
        db,
        entity_type="user",
        entity_id=user.id,
        event_type="auth.logout",
        actor_user_id=user.id,
    )
    db.commit()
    return Response(status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT)

## Google branding sources
- https://developers.google.com/identity/branding-guidelines: light, dark and neutral themes with fills, strokes and text colours, the 12/10/12px padding, the "Sign in with Google" wording, and the rule that the G logo must be the standard colour version and not resized or recoloured.
- https://developers.google.com/identity/gsi/web/reference/html-reference: button type, theme, size and shape options.
- https://developers.google.com/identity/gsi/web/guides/personalized-button: general UX.
- I only got a generic web-search summary of the account-chooser layout, not an official spec. I modelled it on that: title, circular initials avatar, name, email and a vertical list.

Deviations from Google's guidance:
- **Font:** the official page names "Google Sans Medium", not Roboto. The button uses `"Google Sans", Roboto, system-ui`, so nothing is fetched from Google.
- **Size:** the guidelines give no minimum size. I used 40px height and 200px minimum width, matching the Google Identity Services button.
- **Theme:** the button switches between the light and dark variants to follow the app theme.
- **Wording:** the chooser says "Choose a mock account", and there is no "Continue as" text.

## Commands and results
- `bun run lint`, `typecheck` and `build` all pass. `bun run test` runs 18 tests: the 4 theme tests and 14 new auth tests.
- **SSR checks with curl (stub on 9191, built app on 9190):**
  - Unauthenticated `/` returns 302 to `/login`.
  - With a valid cookie, `/` renders "Signed in as Henry Ho (HR Approver)" and the token is not in the HTML.
  - A signed-in user visiting `/login` is redirected to `/`.
  - A 401 from `/me` returns 302 to `/login?reason=expired` and clears the cookie.
- **Browser (Claude Browser pane):**
  - The `/login` warning is visible before any click, and the chooser lists 5 users grouped by role.
  - Focus moves into the dialog and is trapped. Escape, the close button and a backdrop click all close it, and focus returns to the button.
  - Row spinner shown while signing in; other rows are disabled.
  - Error messages for 401, 403, a network failure, an empty list and 404 all show without crashing.
  - Picking a user lands on `/`. A reload keeps the session. Sign out calls the logout endpoint, clears the cookie and returns to `/login`. A forced 401 also signs out.
  - The cookie's Max-Age is about 3600 seconds.
  - Nothing is stored in localStorage or the payload.
  - Console is clean in dev and prod, with no hydration warnings.
  - At 360px width there is no horizontal scroll in light or dark.
- **Contrast** (computed): all text pairs are 4.5:1 or better. That covers the warning in light and dark (14.4 and 13.5), the badges, the red error panel, the avatar initials and the secondary text at 80% opacity. The warning border is 3.07:1 in light, which is non-text and passes the 3:1 rule.

- **Cookie:** it is set from JavaScript, so page scripts can read it. It is not httpOnly, and a httpOnly cookie would need the backend to set it. I kept the JWT out of `useState`, so only the user object goes into the SSR payload.

- **`apiBaseServer`** is a private runtimeConfig key and is read only on the server.
- **Expired notice:** an SSR redirect starts a new request, so I carry the reason in a `?reason=expired` query flag. It is not a token.
- **Cross-tab staleness:** if another tab signs in as a different user, an open tab keeps its old user state until it next reloads or validates. I did not add a fix.
- **Modal detail:** Escape and backdrop clicks are ignored while a sign-in is in flight.

- The backend needs CORS for `http://localhost:9180` with the `Authorization` and `Content-Type` headers, and the POST and GET methods. The browser calls the API cross-origin.

- **New:**

## Google branding sources
- https://developers.google.com/identity/branding-guidelines: light, dark and neutral themes with fills, strokes and text colours, the 12/10/12px padding, the "Sign in with Google" wording, and the rule that the G logo must be the standard colour version and not resized or recoloured.
- https://developers.google.com/identity/gsi/web/reference/html-reference: button type, theme, size and shape options.
- https://developers.google.com/identity/gsi/web/guides/personalized-button: general UX.
- I only got a generic web-search summary of the account-chooser layout, not an official spec. I modelled it on that: title, circular initials avatar, name, email and a vertical list.

Deviations from Google's guidance:
- **Font:** the official page names "Google Sans Medium", not Roboto. The button uses `"Google Sans", Roboto, system-ui`, so nothing is fetched from Google.
- **Size:** the guidelines give no minimum size. I used 40px height and 200px minimum width, matching the Google Identity Services button.
- **Theme:** the button switches between the light and dark variants to follow the app theme.
- **Wording:** the chooser says "Choose a mock account", and there is no "Continue as" text.

## Commands and results
- `bun run lint`, `typecheck` and `build` all pass. `bun run test` runs 18 tests: the 4 theme tests and 14 new auth tests.
- **SSR checks with curl (stub on 9191, built app on 9190):**
  - Unauthenticated `/` returns 302 to `/login`.
  - With a valid cookie, `/` renders "Signed in as Henry Ho (HR Approver)" and the token is not in the HTML.
  - A signed-in user visiting `/login` is redirected to `/`.
  - A 401 from `/me` returns 302 to `/login?reason=expired` and clears the cookie.
- **Browser (Claude Browser pane):**
  - The `/login` warning is visible before any click, and the chooser lists 5 users grouped by role.
  - Focus moves into the dialog and is trapped. Escape, the close button and a backdrop click all close it, and focus returns to the button.
  - Row spinner shown while signing in; other rows are disabled.
  - Error messages for 401, 403, a network failure, an empty list and 404 all show without crashing.
  - Picking a user lands on `/`. A reload keeps the session. Sign out calls the logout endpoint, clears the cookie and returns to `/login`. A forced 401 also signs out.
  - The cookie's Max-Age is about 3600 seconds.
  - Nothing is stored in localStorage or the payload.
  - Console is clean in dev and prod, with no hydration warnings.
  - At 360px width there is no horizontal scroll in light or dark.
- **Contrast** (computed): all text pairs are 4.5:1 or better. That covers the warning in light and dark (14.4 and 13.5), the badges, the red error panel, the avatar initials and the secondary text at 80% opacity. The warning border is 3.07:1 in light, which is non-text and passes the 3:1 rule.
- **Ports:** my servers on 9190, 9191 and 9192 are stopped and those ports are free. Ports 9180 and 9181 are held by pre-existing Docker containers (PID 9781), not mine. I used 9190/9191 for verification instead of stopping them, so I could not confirm 9180/9181 are free.

## Decisions and tradeoffs
- **Cookie:** it is set from JavaScript, so page scripts can read it. It is not httpOnly, and a httpOnly cookie would need the backend to set it. I kept the JWT out of `useState`, so only the user object goes into the SSR payload.
- **Two cookie refs at login:** Nuxt fixes a cookie's maxAge when the ref is created, so login creates a second ref carrying the lifetime from `expires_in`.
- **Nuxt bug avoided:** calling `runWithContext` nested during SSR clears the outer Nuxt context and returns a 500 (E1001). The cookie ref is now created once per Nuxt app, and the context is re-entered only when it is actually missing.
- **`apiBaseServer`** is a private runtimeConfig key and is read only on the server.
- **Expired notice:** an SSR redirect starts a new request, so I carry the reason in a `?reason=expired` query flag. It is not a token.
- **Cross-tab staleness:** if another tab signs in as a different user, an open tab keeps its old user state until it next reloads or validates. I did not add a fix.
- **Modal detail:** Escape and backdrop clicks are ignored while a sign-in is in flight.

## For the integrator and backend
- The backend needs CORS for `http://localhost:9180` with the `Authorization` and `Content-Type` headers, and the POST and GET methods. The browser calls the API cross-origin.
- I assumed all of the contract as given. The frontend drops any user object with an unknown role or missing fields.
- docker-compose already sets `NUXT_API_BASE_SERVER: http://api:9181`, which matches what the frontend expects.
- The stub is at `frontend/scripts/mock-api-stub.ts` (dev aid only, documented in `frontend/README.md`).
- Confirm that the seeded emails and the 3/1/1 employee/HR/finance split are what the backend uses. The stub used Amy Lau, Ben Wong, Chloe Cheung, Henry Ho and Fiona Fung.

# Backend (FastAPI)

Python 3.12 managed by `uv`. Run all commands from `backend/`. Backend port is 9181.
All data is fictional (`@example.com` users, made-up requests).

- Install: `uv sync`
- Test: `uv run pytest -q` (offline; never reads the repo-root `.env`)
- Lint: `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run ruff format --check .`
- Run: `uv run uvicorn app.main:app --port 9181` then `curl localhost:9181/health`
- Config: env vars from the repo-root `.env` (see `../.env.example`); the file may be absent.
- Secrets (`GEMINI_API_KEY`, `REQRES_API_KEY`, `JWT_SECRET_KEY`) are `SecretStr` and never printed.

## Layout

| Path | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `app/db/` | SQLAlchemy models, engine/session (SQLite pragmas), column types |
| `app/domain/` | Pure rules: status state machine, roles, leave day maths (no DB/FastAPI) |
| `app/schemas/` | Pydantic API and draft-input models |
| `app/services/` | DB-aware helpers: audit trail, polymorphic-reference checks, holidays |
| `app/auth/` | JWT create/verify, `get_current_user`, `require_roles` |
| `app/api/routes/` | HTTP routes, mounted under `/api` (`/health` stays at the root) |
| `app/seed.py`, `app/cli.py` | Fictional demo data and the `python -m app.cli` tools |

## Database

SQLite through SQLAlchemy 2.x. Tables are created with `create_all` (no migrations). Every
connection sets `foreign_keys=ON`, `busy_timeout=5000`, `synchronous=NORMAL` and, for file
databases, `journal_mode=WAL`. Timestamps are timezone-aware UTC. Money and day counts are
exact `Decimal` values stored as integers (never floats).

On startup the API creates the tables and, when `DB_AUTO_SEED=true` and the `users` table is
empty, loads the demo data. A startup failure is logged and does not stop the API.

```bash
uv run python -m app.cli init-db
uv run python -m app.cli seed                 # idempotent; no-op if users exist
uv run python -m app.cli seed --reset --yes   # DROP all tables, rebuild, reseed
```

## Auth (mock Google SSO + real JWT)

| Endpoint | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/auth/mock-users` | active seed users (no `google_subject`) |
| `POST /api/auth/mock-google/login` `{"email": "..."}` | `{access_token, token_type, expires_in, user}`; 401 `Invalid credentials`; 403 `Account is inactive` |
| `GET /api/auth/me` (Bearer) | `{id, email, display_name, role}`; 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` |
| `POST /api/auth/logout` (Bearer) | 204 and an `auth.logout` audit row (tokens are stateless; the client discards its token) |

Tokens are HS256 with `sub, email, role, iss, iat, exp, jti`. Only HS256 is accepted (`alg: none`
is rejected). The user, role and `is_active` are re-read from the database on every request, so
the token's role claim is informational only. `MOCK_SSO_ENABLED=false` turns the mock endpoints
into 404. With an empty `JWT_SECRET_KEY` a random per-process secret is used (a warning is
logged); `APP_ENV=production` requires a secret of at least 32 characters.

Seeded fictional users: `amy.lau@`, `ben.chow@`, `cathy.ng@` (employees), `daniel.wong@`
(HR approver), `eva.cheung@` (Finance approver), all at `example.com`.

## Public holidays

Leave working days skip Saturdays, Sundays and rows in `public_holidays`. The seed loads 2026 and
2027 from the bundled `app/data/hk_public_holidays_1823.ics` (snapshot of the official 1823.gov.hk
iCal, fetched 2026-09-25), with source `seed_2026`.

1823 publishes about three years ahead. Each year, once the next calendar appears:

```bash
uv run python -m app.cli import-holidays --year 2028
# or from a downloaded file
uv run python -m app.cli import-holidays --file path/to/en.ics --year 2028
# inside Docker Compose
docker compose exec api python -m app.cli import-holidays --year 2028
```

The command downloads `https://www.1823.gov.hk/common/ical/en.ics` (override with `--url`),
upserts by date (safe to re-run, source `1823_ics`) and prints inserted/updated counts. If a
requested year is not in the feed it exits non-zero with a message and changes nothing.

| `MOCK_SSO_ENABLED` | Enables the mock Google sign-in endpoints (default `true`) |
| `NUXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE` | Backend URL as seen by the browser |""")

new_sections = """## Demo sign-in and seeded users

Open <http://localhost:9180>, click **Sign in with Google**, and pick an account. This is a **mock** sign-in: the page says so before and after the click, nothing is sent to Google, and choosing an account signs you in immediately as that fictional user (no password). Behind it the backend issues a real signed JWT.

| User | Email | Role | Can do (from the next phase) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Amy Lau, Ben Chow, Cathy Ng | `amy.lau@`, `ben.chow@`, `cathy.ng@example.com` | `employee` | Create Leave and Claim requests; view only their own |
| Daniel Wong | `daniel.wong@example.com` | `hr_approver` | List, view, approve, reject Leave requests only |
| Eva Cheung | `eva.cheung@example.com` | `finance_approver` | List, view, approve, reject Claim requests only |

Auth API (mounted under `/api/auth`): `GET /mock-users`, `POST /mock-google/login`, `GET /me`, `POST /logout`. The backend re-reads the user and role from the database on every request, so the role inside the token is never trusted on its own. Details and error codes are in [backend/README.md](backend/README.md).

## Database and seed data

SQLite (WAL mode, foreign keys enforced) through SQLAlchemy, stored in the `api-data` volume. Ten tables: `users`, `conversations`, `conversation_messages`, `leave_requests`, `claim_requests`, `external_submissions`, `notifications`, `audit_events`, `public_holidays`, `feedback`.

| Seed data | Rows | Notes |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Users | 5 | 3 employees, 1 HR approver, 1 Finance approver (`@example.com`) |
| Leave requests | 10 | 2 pending, recent approved and rejected, the rest past history; includes half-day examples |
| Claim requests | 10 | Same mix, HKD amounts |
| Audit events | 15 | Creation, confirmation, API submission, a 429 failure then retry, approval, rejection |
| Conversations | 3 | With 9 short messages |
| Public holidays | 34 | Hong Kong 2026 and 2027 (17 each) |

Also seeded: 21 external-submission records, 6 notifications and 2 feedback rows. Every seeded record is fictional. Rebuild the demo data at any time:

```bash
docker compose exec api python -m app.cli seed --reset --yes   # drops and reseeds the database
```

**Request status flow** (enforced in the backend): `draft` → `pending_approval` (after confirmation and API submission) or `submission_failed` (retry allowed) → `approved` or `rejected`; `draft` and `submission_failed` can also be `cancelled`. Rejecting needs a reviewer note, and a reviewer cannot act on their own request. HR reviews Leave only; Finance reviews Claims only.

**Half-day leave.** `leave_requests` has `start_day_part` and `end_day_part` (`full`, `am`, `pm`), and `working_days` is a decimal in 0.5 steps.

| Request | start / end date | start_day_part / end_day_part | working_days |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| Whole day | same date | `full` / `full` | 1 |
| Half day, morning or afternoon | same date | `am` / `am` or `pm` / `pm` | 0.5 |
| Several days, starting at noon | different dates | `pm` / `full` | first day counts 0.5 |
| Several days, ending at noon | different dates | `full` / `am` | last day counts 0.5 |

The working week is Monday to Friday, excluding Hong Kong public holidays. Those two optional fields are all the chat step needs to fill for "half day tomorrow afternoon".

### Hong Kong public holidays: yearly update

The 2026 and 2027 holidays are bundled from the official 1823 calendar (checked against the gov.hk holiday pages on 2026-09-25). 1823 publishes roughly three years ahead, so each year, once the new year appears, import it:

```bash
docker compose exec api python -m app.cli import-holidays --year 2028
# local (no Docker), from backend/
uv run python -m app.cli import-holidays --year 2028
# offline, from a downloaded calendar file
uv run python -m app.cli import-holidays --file path/to/en.ics --year 2028
```

The import is safe to re-run (it updates by date), and it stops with a clear message if the year is not yet published.

## Testing

Tests run locally, not inside Docker. Docker Compose is only used to run and demonstrate the stack.

| What | Command | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Backend unit tests (205, offline) | `cd backend && uv run pytest -q` | local |
| Backend lint | `cd backend && uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .` | local |
| Frontend lint, types, unit tests (18) | `cd frontend && bun run lint && bun run typecheck && bun run test` | local |
| Full-stack smoke check | `docker compose up --build`, then open both URLs above | Docker |

Backend tests use in-memory or temporary SQLite databases, never read `.env`, and never call ReqRes or Gemini.

"""
s=s.replace("## Local development (without Docker)", new_sections+"## Local development (without Docker)")
open(p,"w").write(s)
PYEOF
grep -n '^## \|^### ' README.md

Phase 1 is finished and committed locally (4 commits, nothing pushed). I left the new stack running at <http://localhost:9180> so you can test.

**What I checked**
- **Backend:** 205 tests pass and ruff is clean.
- **Frontend:** lint, typecheck and 18 tests pass.
- **In Docker:** I signed in as Daniel Wong (HR) in the browser pane.
  - `/` redirected to `/login`.
  - The mock warning showed before I clicked, and again inside the chooser.
  - After sign-in, a hard reload kept the session.
  - The page HTML and browser storage contained no token, the dark theme worked, and sign-out cleared the cookie.
- **Not done:** I did not test signing in as an employee or the Finance approver in the browser. Those logins are only covered by the backend tests.

**Your ten points**
1. **Models and tables:** all 10 tables are in SQLAlchemy with your column lists. SQLite runs in WAL mode with foreign keys enforced, and constraints reject bad roles and statuses.
2. **Half-day leave:** I added `start_day_part` and `end_day_part` (`full`, `am`, `pm`) to `leave_requests`, so `working_days` moves in 0.5 steps. The rules and examples are in the README. The working week is Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
3. **Seed data:**
   - Counts: 5 users, 10 leave, 10 claims, 15 audit events (including a 429 failure then a successful retry), 3 conversations.
   - Also seeded: 21 external-submission records, 6 notifications and 2 feedback rows.
4. **Holidays:**
   - 2026 and 2027 have 17 dates each, from the official 1823 calendar. I checked them against the gov.hk pages and they matched.
   - The yearly command is `docker compose exec api python -m app.cli import-holidays --year 2028`, and it is in the README.
   - Right now the 1823 feed only covers up to 2027.
5. **Tests:** roles, state transitions, half-day maths, seed counts and the auth API are covered, and all run offline.
6. **Sign-in UI:** it follows Google's branding guidelines, with the mock warning and an account chooser for the 5 users.
7. **Real JWT:** the four sign-in endpoints are live. The user and role are re-read from the database on every request, so a demoted user loses access immediately.
8. **Testing (your question 4):** tests run locally, and Docker is only for running the stack. This is now in the README.

**Things to know or decide**
- **Raw values in the database:** the backend agent stored `working_days` as integer tenths (a half day shows as `5`) and money as cents. The values are correct through the API, but they look confusing if you open the SQLite file. Say if you want readable values instead; it's a small change.
- **Your Phase 0 containers:** I stopped them because they held ports 9180 and 9181, then rebuilt on the Phase 1 code.
- **JWT secret:** `JWT_SECRET_KEY` is empty in `.env`, so logins reset whenever the API restarts. For a stable local setup, put `openssl rand -hex 32` in `.env`. I did not touch `.env`.
- **Cookie:** the token is stored in a cookie set from JavaScript, so it is not `httpOnly`. A `httpOnly` cookie would need the backend to set it; I can do that later.
- **Prompt log:** entries 05–08 in `PROMPT-INSTRUCTION.md` cover this phase. Every agent reported Sonnet 5.

Test it at <http://localhost:9180>. When you're ready, tell me what to build for the roles.

content.content:
# One Tap User Experience Overview

## Display & Appearance
The One Tap prompt appears as a consent dialog showing the user's Google account. For returning users, it displays an account selection interface with a "Continue as" button. Users can close it via a close button in the top-right corner. On non-Chromium browsers, a secondary pop-up dialog reinforces account creation consent.

## When It Appears
One Tap displays only when there's "at least one active session on Google websites." It won't show if the user has opted out globally through Google Account settings or disabled third-party sign-in in browser settings.

## Cooldown Behavior
When users manually close the prompt, it triggers exponential suppression periods:
- 1st close: Two hours
- 2nd close: One day
- 3rd close: One week
- 4th+ close: Four weeks

"Auto-dismissal doesn't trigger a cooldown." Successful sign-in resets this timer.

## Mobile Auto-Dismissal
"On mobile browsers, and when FedCM is not enabled, Google One Tap closes automatically after a short time period unless the user directly interacts with the One Tap UI." The threshold is 90 seconds. Desktop and tablet experiences don't auto-dismiss.

## FedCM Impact
With Federated Credential Manager enabled, "browser vendors may define their own, different, cooldown time periods." Chrome users can reset permissions via the address bar lock icon. The core UI transitions to browser-native credential selection interfaces rather than Google-hosted dialogs.

## ITP Browsers
On Safari, Firefox, and Chrome iOS, the experience begins with a welcome page before opening a pop-up window for sign-in.

content.content:
# Cross-Account Protection (RISC) Summary

## Overview
Cross-Account Protection delivers "cryptographically signed security event tokens to an endpoint you set up" to notify apps of major Google Account changes affecting user security.

## Supported Security Events

Google sends the following event types:

1. **`sessions-revoked`** – End all active user sessions immediately
2. **`tokens-revoked`** – Terminate sessions (if Google Sign-in) or delete stored OAuth tokens
3. **`token-revoked`** – Delete corresponding refresh tokens and request user re-consent
4. **`account-disabled`** (reasons: hijacking, bulk-account) – End sessions for hijacking; analyze activity for bulk-account cases
5. **`account-enabled`** – Re-enable Sign-in and account recovery
6. **`account-credential-change-required`** – Monitor for suspicious activity
7. **`verification`** – Log test token receipt

## Receiver Endpoint Mechanism

The receiver handles "HTTPS POST requests" containing signed JWTs. Apps must:

- **Validate**: Verify signature using Google's public key, confirm audience (client ID) and issuer claims
- **Decode**: Extract event type and affected user's Google Account ID
- **Respond**: Return HTTP 202 and take appropriate security actions
- **Deduplicate**: Use the `jti` claim to prevent processing duplicate events

## Key Constraint
"These signals may only be used for security, anti-fraud, and session management purposes."

content.content:
# Google ID Token Backend Verification

## Required Verification Steps

According to the documentation, backends must verify:

1. **Signature**: "The ID token is properly signed by Google. Use Google's public keys (available in JWK or PEM format) to verify the token's signature."

2. **Standard Claims**:
   - `iss` equals `accounts.google.com` or `https://accounts.google.com`
   - `aud` matches your app's client ID(s)
   - `exp` has not passed

3. **Additional Claims**: The `hd` (hosted domain) claim helps identify Google Workspace accounts.

## ID Token Lifetime

The document does **not** specify an explicit token lifetime duration. It only requires checking that "The expiry time (`exp`) of the ID token has not passed."

## Sub vs. Email as Identifier

The guidance is emphatic: "Only use Google ID token `sub` field as identifier for the user as it is unique among all Google Accounts and never reused."

The documentation specifically warns: "Email is not a good choice because it can be changed by the user" and recommends storing the `sub` field "and associate it with the user in your account management system."

While email can be used to check for existing accounts, it should never serve as the primary identifier due to its mutability.
